Got it guys! Fantastic conversation here! To further on this conversation. Once you identified the limits of the flag you look for how price is approaching those limits. If it CP's to the limit, short it right away! If there is a rocket into the level, watch for an engulf first. Don't trade in the middle of these limits unless you are looking at smaller time frames for flag limits to get engulfed and you are going in the direction of the trend and trading on smaller time frames to get to the limits of the larger time frames.

I hope this all made sense to everybody.

Here's something I'm currently getting a sore head with.

There is a lovely flagged area on the EURUSD 4hr, which I have drawn in with a green rectangle, and projected forwards. The top of this is also the weekly close. As marked on the chart, this seems to be a flip area, and looks to now act as a supply area. It is also the DP for a strong move up, recently ignored.

However, on the LTF I see that price has engulfed a flag to the upside, and may be about to go higher. This is my number one issue with SD trading - not finding clear enough setups so that the LTF backs up the HTF. Frustration abounds.

As this Decision Point has no nearby FTR, could the price action right now be considered the FTR for this DP?

Does this look like a valid QM? Is there any significance to the 2 precise 1.28380 points? Is this consumption of sell orders, so diminishing supply? Is the way to approach this to wait for a more definitive engulf of what is now essentially a bigger flag between my 1min grey box and the QM LL? That does seem the safest way to go, if I'm honest with myself.

Should I give any weight to the classic ascending triangle this is forming.

Thanks, everyone.

Welcome to the wonderful world of S/D trading. The questions we run through our minds can be our own worst enemy. No matter what decision we make someone else has a reason to make the opposite, or how would your position be put in place? It just comes down to who will win the buyers or sellers? Trading currencies is like a tug-o-war. The entire side loses that is weaker. So our only job is to find the strong side and jump on.

I don't have the time to answer all your questions, besides some of them will get into my opinion to much. To me with trading there is loads of opinion and we don't know who was right till the "Rope" is pulled across the line.

To me the 4hr zone you have marked is messy. If I were to place a pending order it would be at the blue dotted line. Keep in mind though; I don't place to many pending orders right now.

More important to me is the PA further left.

Interesting chart though if you look at the Daily. How far is the potential drop if the H&S rules hold true?

One more thing. If I am looking at a 4hr chart I will usually drop no more then 2 time frames to get a grip on PA. Keep in mind you have 240 minute candles for a 4hr candle. Sometimes it will confuse the issue with so much information. Don't get me wrong though at times you can find the exact decision point right down to the pip with the minute chart. But to each his own.
